newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD finance expert calls for EMU flexibility.
newsitem.headline: SPD finance expert calls for EMU flexibility.

text.p: An opposition finance expert said on Tuesday it would be a mistake to apply European monetary union criteria strictly, in the light of efforts Germany and other countries were making to qualify.

In an interview with Deutschland Radio, Social Democrat (SPD) Ingrid Matthaeus-Maier pleaded said the leeway allowed under the Maastricht Treaty should be used in deciding which countries join EMU at the scheduled start in 1999.
"I think it would be a mistake to raise the disciplinary pressure after all countries have undertaken great efforts," she said.
She also said delaying the launch of a single currency would endanger European unity and weaken Germany's image.
"You have to try to achieve the numbers. You have to try to save and to fight unemployment," she said.
"We need the currency union not only politically but also economically," she said.

Mattaeus-Maier also blamed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition for doing too little to lower unemployment while trimming budgets to qualify for EMU. "The government is saving in a way so that unemployment is rising furhter," she said.
